content.rendered:
For all of the incredible songs that came out of Bruce’s prolific songwriting for The River, there were a lot that never went anywhere–including a trifle called “Love’s Gonna Be Tonight.”

As far as we know, “Love’s Gonna Be Tonight” never made it passed the home demo stage, and even those recordings were little more than attempts by Bruce to get his Buddy Holly on.

There’s definitely an infectious “Peggy Sue” vibe to this one in both the melody and lyrics (the few that aren’t bluffed, that is). Take a listen and hear for yourself.

It would have been interesting to hear this one develop; I think it might have been right at home on The River alongside “Two Hearts,” especially in this second attempt, in which we can clearly hear Bruce envisioning what the song would sound like electrified:

But unfortunately, these two very rough and early takes are the only insight we have in to what could have grown into a terrific song if Bruce had only pursued it.

Love’s Gonna Be Tonight
Recorded: Autumn 1979 (demo only)
Never released
Never performed

© September 17, 2019

excerpt.rendered: Cast off before he ever even finished it, “Love’s Gonna Be Tonight” is a Buddy Holly homage that might have been right at home on The River.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Love’s on the Line
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Bruce's original River-era composition, a stellar E Street Band performance and Gary's passionate vocals make for a standout track on an album full of them.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Roll of the Dice: A Night with the Jersey Devil
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A curiosity of a song with an unusual release history. "A Night with the Jersey Devil" is an exercise in clever misdirection, and a sly wink from Bruce.

jetpack-related-posts.title: I’m Gonna Treat You Right (Wild Kisses)
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A true flash in the wild: the E Street Band rehearses a one-time-only performance of a lost, light Springsteen original.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Roll of the Dice: Seaside Bar Song
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: An early Wild and Innocent outtake based on a still-standing bar bears the seeds of classic songs still to come.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Roll of the Dice: In Michigan
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In a bolt of pre-show inspiration, Bruce wrote one of his all-time greatest songs for an appreciative Michigan audience.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Roll of the Dice: Countin’ on a Miracle
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: "Countin' on a Miracle" is a heartbreaking tale of love and loss, one of the most powerful songs on The Rising--but even more powerful still in its alternate post-concert arrangement. Listen to both inside, along with insights and great performances.
